intent: The World Diabetes Day map: not the United States but China, home to a quarter of all adults with diabetes — three countries compared side by side, the global count climbing past half a billion with half undiagnosed, and the Toronto pin for the doctor whose birthday the day marks.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: In which country do MOST people with diabetes live?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: In which country do most people with diabetes live?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: China. About 148 million adults there live with diabetes, 1 in 4 of all cases on Earth.

lines.direction: pull back so China and India share the frame; India lights dim with its tag on 'India'; the three compare blocks rise on 'second' — China, India, United States; the flag-ball shrug on 'States'
lines.text: India is second with about 90 million. The United States has 38 million.

lines.direction: pull right out to the world; the counter climbs to 589 million from 'worldwide'; the globe sticker on 'billion'; the question-mark sticker and a pulse on 'know'
lines.text: Worldwide it is well over half a billion people, and around half of them do not yet know they have it.

lines.direction: swing the camera across to Toronto; the 14 NOV card on 'November'; the Toronto pin and tag on 'birthday'; the syringe sticker and the thinking flag-ball on 'insulin'
lines.text: The 14th of November is World Diabetes Day, the birthday of the doctor who helped discover insulin.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
